6 copy-paste prompts that turn messy meeting notes, emails or drafts into a client-ready report using ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: summarize, structure, fix the tone, check for gaps, write the headline, and proofread.

slides.title: prompts that turn messy notes into a client-ready report
slides.sub: Paste your notes, chat, or email thread — copy, paste, done.
slides.voiceover: Six prompts that turn messy notes into a report you can actually send a client.

slides.name: The Summarizer
slides.sub: Condense a wall of raw notes into the points that matter.
slides.prompt: Here are my raw notes from [MEETING/EMAIL THREAD/CALL]: [PASTE NOTES]. Summarize the key points in plain language, grouped by topic, and flag anything that sounds like a decision or an action item.
slides.voiceover: One. Paste your raw notes and get the key points, grouped by topic.

slides.name: The Structurer
slides.sub: Turn scattered bullet points into a real report layout.
slides.prompt: Using the summary above, structure it into a short report with these sections: Overview, Key Findings, Decisions Made, Next Steps. Keep each section to a few sentences or bullet points, written for [CLIENT/TEAM/MANAGER].
slides.tip: Name the exact audience — a client report and an internal update should read differently.
slides.voiceover: Two. Turn those bullet points into a report with real sections.

slides.name: The Tone Fixer
slides.sub: Rewrite it so it sounds right for who's reading it.
slides.prompt: Rewrite the report above in a [FORMAL/FRIENDLY/CONCISE] tone suitable for [AUDIENCE, e.g. a client who wasn't in the meeting]. Keep every fact the same — only change the wording and tone.
slides.voiceover: Three. Fix the tone for the exact person who's going to read it.

slides.name: The Gap Checker
slides.sub: Catch the missing pieces before you hit send.
slides.prompt: Review the report above and list any missing information, unclear numbers, or unanswered questions a reader would likely ask. For each gap, suggest exactly what to add or who to ask.
slides.tip: Run this before every report — it catches what you skipped because you were too close to the topic.
slides.voiceover: Four. Ask what's missing before your reader has to ask you.

slides.name: The Headline Writer
slides.sub: One line that tells a busy reader what matters most.
slides.prompt: Write a one-sentence executive summary for the report above that a busy [CLIENT/MANAGER] could read in five seconds and understand the outcome. Then suggest a clear title for the report.

lines: Summary: On track, one blocker on [X].

slides.voiceover: Five. Get a one-line summary a busy reader can grab in five seconds.

slides.name: The Proofreader
slides.sub: One last pass for clarity, grammar and consistency.
slides.prompt: Proofread the full report above. Fix grammar, tighten long sentences, make headings and formatting consistent, and flag any sentence that could be misread. Show only the corrected version.
slides.tip: Ask it to also check that names, dates and numbers match your original notes — AI can tighten wording but won't verify facts for you.
slides.voiceover: Six. One last pass for grammar, clarity and consistent formatting.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: Paste your original notes and the report in the same chat so later prompts can check back against them.
ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini all accept documents like PDFs, Word files and text files — skip retyping.
These prompts fix structure and wording, not accuracy — always check names, numbers and dates before sending.
slides.voiceover: Keep your notes in the same chat, upload files directly, and always check the facts yourself.
